_comment: THE cross-language log level window contract. Go (agent-shim/logging/go,
imported by the daemon, the store and the sidecar), TypeScript
(agent-shim/logging/ts/level-window.ts, imported by the shim and the
webapp) and elisp (core.el) each assert their own selection against this
file, so the six runtimes cannot disagree about whether a leftover
setting is honored.
A LEVEL OTHER THAN INFO IS A WINDOW, NEVER A STANDING SETTING.
AGENT_REPL_LOG_LEVEL selects debug, warn or error only together with
AGENT_REPL_LOG_LEVEL_UNTIL, the Unix second (decimal integer) the window
ends at, no more than window_seconds after the runtime reads it. Without
an unexpired, in-window UNTIL the runtime starts at info and says so at
info. A runtime whose window ends while it runs reverts to info by itself
and records the revert at info. A debug level left in a launchd
environment therefore never outlives its five minutes: every runtime that
starts later comes up at info.
An unrecognized level or an UNTIL that is not a decimal integer is a
startup refusal, as an unrecognized level always was.
Each case reads the two variables at instant now (Unix seconds); a null
level or until is a variable that is not set. until_effective is
the window's end, null when the runtime has no window. outcome names the
decision: default (nothing asked for), honored, no_expiry, expired,
beyond_window, or refused.
